recipes.name: Apricot Lentil Soup
ingredients_raw: 3 roma (plum) tomatoes - peeled, seeded and chopped

steps.text: Sauté apricots, onion, and garlic in olive oil, about 5 minutes. Add chicken stock and lentils and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes and season with cumin, thyme, salt, and pepper to taste. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice. Purée 1/2 of the soup in a blender, then return to the pot. Serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Apricot Lentil Soup
raw_recipe.description: This puréed apricot and lentil soup is made with red lentils, dried apricots, and tomatoes cooked in a chicken broth flavored with chicken and thyme.

review.reviewBody: So good. Per the suggestions of others I wanted to add a whole grain with the lentils. I threw in about a half cup of dry rinsed quinoa -wonder food!! I also 2x the spices and garlic, reduced the oil to 1-2 tsp, and because I like a heartier soup, I added 1 sweet potato, cubed and then roughly mashed to the consistency I wanted. This soup was sooo good, and so good for you. A perfect meal. Enjoy.

This recipe was fabulous with some tweaking. I increased the apricots to 1/2 cup, diced, used 1/2 cup red lentils and the rest regular brown to make 2 cups, plus added 1/2 tsp. each of curry pwdr, cardomom, and ground coriander. Because we are vegan, I used 6 cups vegetarian chick'n broth (to compensate for the additional lentils), and then cooked it in a pressure cooker for 15 minutes. After that, I stirred in the lemon juice, and 1 can of diced tomatoes NOT drained, and added salt, and 1 tsp. sugar. PERFECT! What a review it received from my out of town guests! My husband asked if we could have it once a week from now on. I highly recommend giving this soup a try, especially if you have a pressure cooker-the flavor is deep and throughout.

I did like this recipe but i instantly made some changes. First I used coconut oil to sauté the onions and garlic. I doubled this recipe. I cooked and drained the entire bag of red lentils. I used a can of stewed tomatoes. Instead of removing 1/2 and blending I used a hand blender to make creamy. It is now a charming warm and delicate course to enhance a much richer Entrée.

Very good. I used petite diced tomatoes in a can instead of finding the tomatoes. I didn't blend as instructed. I ate it over some brown rice and realized that I should have chopped up the apricots to spread out the flavor because that extra tang was delicious. Once I found my handheld blender, I completed the last steps. ThenI was like oh now I see what everyone is raving about. I would suggest using more than a 1/3 cup of apricots, though. Instead a a half cup and I would double on the seasonings. Really, it is good as is, but I would likely add some spinach to the next time around and I will alternate it with quinoa and brown rice. The rice is good for fiber, but the quinoa provides more protein..
 (Update) I did it for the third time but I used organic vegetable stock from whole foods, and I let the lentils sit in water for two hours. This time the consistency was more like a soup because when I used the dry lentils they would soak up the stock. Also the seasoning in the vegetable stock just gives it more flavor. I would recommend vegetable stock over chicken.

REALLY GOOD!! this is a great recipe for lentils. i used green lentils, doubled the spices, used cherry tomatoes seeds and all, and doubled the lemon juice. Don't skip the lemon juice because it really adds a great flavor. i also used 1/2 cup of apricots and chopped them up in my bullet to very small pieces..it worked perfectly. Lastly, I did puree 1/2 the soup in my bullet just before serving and found that to be very important to give the soup some body. i will be making this recipe for many more dinners!!! loved it!!

I came across this recipe in my ongoing quest to find foods for someone on a pureed diet. Potato, cream, and cheese based soups were getting a bit old, and pureed bean in general doesn't really need to be soup. This one seemed different without being off the rails. SUCCESS! Another soup to add to the arsenal. I was worried about the apricot, but read the reviews and was careful not to add too much. Since the recipe doesn't say what to do with the apricot, I diced them fairly small, and measured that way. The taste was very slight, but enough to give it character. I didn't peel the tomatoes either. Only one tablespoon of lemon, and I thought it was way more than enough. Red lentils are kind of important as they break down better. Found them at Sprouts whole foods. I used a stick blender to puree the whole batch, and it made a wonderfully thick, tasty soup, perfect for what I was looking for. Good protein and fiber are a bonus!

sautéed onions til almost carmelized, tripled spices as used water in place of broth to make it vegetarian, added both aleppo pepper and cayenne, used can diced tomatoes
did not need to blend

diced the apricots--they plump up 
think I'd add a tad more lentils next time

Very good! When adding the tomatoes, I put them directly into the blender with the half of the soup so that they got fully emulsified into the soup. I doubled the amount of cumin and thyme. I also added 1 cup of 2% milk. It makes enough for a family meal, or plenty of leftovers if you're a single person.

I made enough for 8 servings. Used veggie broth for my vegetarian friends. Added 3/4 cup quinoa. 2 tsps. of the spices. Accidentally poured way too much black pepper in but that actually gave it a good flavor. The quinoa seemed to soak up the juice so I added approx 2 more cups of broth after pureeing. Also added a bit of cayenne pepper.
It was very good, but, I think the chicken broth might have more flavor.

This is great! I can't wait to eat it tomorrow, when it's had a chance to get even better. I doubled the cumin, but kept the thyme at 1/2 tsp. I also used veggie broth, since I'm a vegetarian. I didn't seed or peel the tomatoes and didn't blend half of the soup. It was still great. A real keeper!

Delicious! I used 1 1/2 c. petite diced tomatoes, which I added with lentils and vegetable broth. After reading other reviews, I upped the cumin to 1 tsp. and added one diced sweet potato. Simmering all ingredients together, I needed to add 2-3 c. water, but it was still very thick and tasty. My family enjoyed it.

Delicious! I make this one regularly. The recipe doesn't mention it, but I think that the apricots should be chopped up first. I used canned tomatoes and added some chopped carrots, chickpeas and more cumin. I have been eating this for lunch with some french bread for a week and I am still looking forward to the next meal.
This was exceptionally tasty. I would never have thought of incorporating apricots into a lentil soup. This is definitely a keeper!
One of our favorites. I used green lentils, but I think red is better. I also add a bit more cumin and thyme. Don't forget the lemon juice.

This was delicious! I made half a recipe, for just me and my husband. I used a beefsteak tomato instead of Roma and added a bit more chicken stock than called for, as it was a bit thick for us otherwise. I added a drizzle of fresh olive oil that my husband brought back from Italy, that was made from the olives of his mother's olive tree! Buonissimo!
I make this almost weekly. It’s delicious! I use a can of diced tomatoes to make it easier and double the apricots. Enjoy!

This is my new favorite soup! There is so much flavor, texture and depth to it. Each bite had a little something different. It was tangy, a little sweet, earthy and very fragrant. 

The only changes I made were to add canned tomatoes (it's what I had on hand) and homemade vegetable stock. 

I will be making this for years to come.
Outstanding taste!

I used vegetable stock, added a cubed sweet pototoe, 1/2 cup of quinoa and doubled the cumin and garlic. I did not have fresh tomato so I used a large can of cubed tomato. 
I also increased the stock by one cup.
I served it with toasted naan bread. Yum! 
Everyone loved it and wanted it added to the rotation.

I've been making this soup for over 20 years, after finding the recipe in a newspaper cooking section as 'Armenian Lentil and Apricot Soup'. Even people who dislike the sludginess of lentils rave about this. It's a breeze for the cook. You can whip this up in less than an hour.

I use pretty much the same recipe as the original poster with these modifications:

1. If fresh tomatoes are not available or if I'm feeling lazy, I'll substitute a can of Ro-Tel diced tomatoes and green chiles. Perfect! (It does well with a spicier touch.)

2. I'll use 10-12 dried half-apricots, dicing them or cutting them into strips.

3. If short on apricots, I'll augment the flavor with apricot preserves, using up to 1/4 cup.

4. Brown-green lentils pack a bit more protein than the red, and are just as tasty as the red ones. However, if presentation is your concern, red lentils make for a much prettier soup.

Gee, I feel like making another batch, right now!
